A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeCoFlow research. All 18 pages, including equations, figures, tables and references, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeCoFlow experiments on MVTec-AD and VisA, including detection, localization, forgetting, component ablations and mechanism analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports an EVA02-B14 image-level detection result in Section 5.2.

M1.justification: The frozen-base and task-specific adapter decomposition, TSA, ACL, TAL, routing and anomaly-scoring procedures in Sections 3–4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate anomaly detection and localization on MVTec-AD and VisA, retaining the same continual-learning scenarios, including the diagnostic mixed-class test. No dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 is unchanged. EVA02-B14 and ViT-B/8 already appear in v1's backbone comparison.

E3.justification: The reported learning orders, training budgets, resolutions, model configurations and evaluation procedures are unchanged. The additional EVA02-B14 score does not document a new protocol or a change in settings.

E4.justification: The component and factorial ablations, backbone/resolution comparisons, routing tests and mechanism analyses are retained. The EVA02-B14 addition supplies another score for an existing comparison without introducing a new analytical question or test.

E5.justification: Three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting, Table 6 variability measures, and the Welch's t-test in Section 5.4 are unchanged. No new uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports EVA02-B14's VisA I-AUC as 95.77%; v1 reported only its P-AP of 44.01%, which is retained. ViT-B/8's P-AP remains 38.05%. This is an additional result for an existing backbone comparison, not a revision of Table 2's 93.00% ViT-B/16 result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, subnet-independence proposition and correct-routing forgetting corollary are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about structural isolation, compensatory modules and zero forgetting under correct routing. Headline I-AUC claims remain 98.40% on MVTec-AD and 93.00% on VisA.

C2.justification: The interpretation of VisA localization weaknesses as a feature-granularity issue is retained. Mechanism explanations and limitations concerning mixed-class learning, routing overlap and longer streams are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training and inference resource information, and the code-access link are unchanged. No additional implementation details accompany the newly reported EVA02-B14 score.

R1.justification: The same 42 references and related-work discussion are retained, with no change in novelty positioning or relationships to prior methods.

P1.justification: Section 5.2 locally revises the backbone-results sentence to state explicit I-AUC/P-AP labels. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, captions, formatting and placement. The short prose edit causes only incidental line reflow.

improvement.justification: Reporting both detection I-AUC and localization P-AP for EVA02-B14 makes the existing VisA backbone comparison slightly more informative, while explicit metric labels improve clarity. The benefit is limited to reporting completeness; the main experimental evidence, reproducibility information and stated limitations remain unchanged.
